title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript note. It is a typed page (p. 113, Exposé IX) from Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §9.4. It appears to have been filed in the archive among the 1975-76 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, and has nothing to do with the neighbouring pages on coalgebras, comodules and hyperalgebras.

Setting (9.4.7.3): the statement 9.4.7, on extending isomorphisms of 'extensions panachées' from the generic point η, is generalised from a trait (a discrete valuation ring) to any connected regular noetherian scheme S of dimension 1, i.e. a Dedekind scheme. In that case one takes a pairing Q_s ⊗ Q_s* → Λ_s at each closed point s.

Proof, part a). An extension panachée X has a filtration with graded pieces Q, ..., P (in the notation of SGA 7 IX, 9.3). Its endomorphisms, or the automorphisms inducing the identity on the graded pieces, are given by sections of the sheaf Hom(P,Q). This sheaf is represented by D(Q⊗Q*), the Cartier dual, which is finite over S.
- Since S is normal, every section over η of a finite S-scheme extends uniquely to S. The scheme-theoretic closure of the generic section is integral, finite and birational over S, hence isomorphic to S.
- So End(X) → End(X_η) is bijective.
- The same holds for the Hom (in fact Isom) sheaf between two extensions that are already known to be isomorphic, since it is then a torsor under the previous group.

Proof, part b). One wants every isomorphism X_η ≅ Y_η to come from an isomorphism X ≅ Y.
- By a), uniqueness and gluing make the question local for the étale topology, so one reduces to S strictly local.
- There, 9.4.3 identifies Ext^1_Λ(P,Q) → Ext^1_Λ(P_η,Q_η) with V*⊗Ȟ_0 → K*⊗Ȟ_0, where V is a lattice/integral module and K its generic counterpart.
- The argument continues on the next typescript page, which is not provided here.

The page serves the proof of the orthogonality and extension results for Néron models and monodromy (Grothendieck's pairing), within the theory of mixed extensions / biextensions.
errors: The 'Hom(X,Y)' in a) should be read as the sheaf of isomorphisms; it is a torsor once X and Y are known to be isomorphic. This is consistent with the text's own hypothesis.
The page is misfiled relative to its neighbours: it is SGA 7 typescript, not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes.

ideas.what: Generic isomorphisms of extensions panachées over a Dedekind base extend uniquely. Uniqueness uses normality of S and finiteness of the Cartier dual D(Q⊗Q*); existence uses étale localisation and an Ext^1 computation.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of isomorphisms of mixed extensions / biextensions; Néron-model and monodromy pairing theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I, Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: A section over the generic point of a finite scheme over a normal base extends uniquely.
ideas.modern_name: Valuative/normality extension of sections of finite schemes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, so its content is fully in the literature and credited to Grothendieck. Its only interest is as an archival misfiling.
transcription_corrections: The 'Hom' in 'Hom(X,Y) → Hom(X_η, Y_η)' and in 'Hom(P,Q)' is underlined in the original, meaning the sheaf Hom; the transcription renders this correctly.
The page number '431' appears twice in the transcription (a pencil archive mark and a printed folio); the content is the same.
The marginal pencil '153' at bottom left is the archive page number and is not part of the text.
